title: sign(): unconditional CRLF after content_mime doubles CRLF
description:
smime-tree/src/sign.rs appends unconditional 
 after content_mime. RFC 2046 §5.1.1: CRLF before boundary belongs to boundary delimiter, not part body. When content_mime already ends with 
 (as all well-formed MIME parts do), output has double 

 before second boundary. OpenSSL tolerates this but it is non-standard. Fix: only append 
 if content_mime does not already end with it.
close_reason: Empirically verified as non-issue: the unconditional CRLF is RFC-conformant. RFC 2046 §5.1.1 explicitly requires two CRLFs before the boundary when content ends with CRLF — one from the body, one from the boundary delimiter. Tests confirm.
